messages:
jess: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression after the new soft-cap admission patch on canary. p99 gen latency +12% on small requests. Posting logs and a quick hypothesis.
perf-bot: [automated] canary-deploy 2026-03-15T10:12:34Z completed, metrics snapshot attached. No infra alerts.
sam: I see the same in staging traces. KV hit ratio dipped ~6% and avg batch token count shortened. Might be more fragmented batches.
maria: can you paste the profiler tail / relevant logs? small snippets are enough.
jess: snippet pasted below:
```
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] batch_assembly: avg_batch_tokens=42 -> 28
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] kv_prefetch: miss_rate=0.18 -> 0.27
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] kernel_select: chosen_kernel=wave (fallback from fused) for sequences<=32
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] admission: softcap_triggered=true, token_budget_remaining=5
```
sam: interesting — kernel switch to "wave" at small batch sizes could add overhead per-batch. If batches collapse under the softcap we might be repeatedly incurring recompile/context cost.
nate: another angle: token_budget target is currently 64. If admission is too aggressive, we prematurely shed tokens and force smaller batches. Suggest trying token_budget=80 for a canary.
maria: also noticed the admission leaky-bucket decay is 0.2 in this roll — that aggressively drops the rolling available tokens, so a short burst will fragment afterwards. Increasing decay (slower leak) might keep batch aggregation stable.
jess: agreed. Proposed canary experiment:
  - A: force kernel_hint=fused for batches <=48 (sam)
  - B: token_budget=80 (nate)
  - C: prefetch window 15ms -> 30ms to reduce KV miss-induced stalls (maria)
  - D: enable perf-bot extra counters: per-batch kernel_choice, kv_trace_id, batch_latency_components (perf-bot)
sam: I'll run A/B forked canary today and collect p50/p90/p99 + kv hit traces. Will add a perf dashboard.
perf-bot: [automated] started trace collection for trace-set id=canary-1757777000.
jess: also let's add a temporary alert rule: p99 latency delta > 8% vs baseline for any prod route should trigger automatic rollback of the softcap change. :eyes:
nate: ack, will add rollback rule to rollout policy.
maria: small note — if fused kernel is faster for small seqs, we need to make sure kernel selector uses batch_token_count hint instead of absolute batch count; otherwise longer sequences could pick bad kernels.
sam: good call. I'll instrument kernel selector to log both batch_token_count and max_seq_len for a short window.
jess: thanks everyone. If A/B shows improvement we'll bake adjustments into the softcap policy (decay/token targets) and land a tuned rollout. Otherwise we revert.
sam: posting initial numbers once canary finishes (ETA ~2h).
jess: great — please ping #eng-runtime if anything surprising. :thumbsup:
